name: Augmented-Forest-Segmentation
description: This dataset contains satellite/aerial images paired with a text prompt instructing to segment the forest area, along with corresponding binary segmentation masks. It evaluates image semantic segmentation of forest regions in remote sensing imagery.
card_text: The dataset consists of 186 samples of image-text pairs. Each sample includes an input satellite or aerial image (JPG), a short natural language prompt such as 'Segment out the forest area in the image', and an output binary mask image (JPG) highlighting forest regions. The imagery is typical of remote sensing scenes, with natural landscapes and varying forest coverage. The task requires pixel-level classification of forest versus non-forest. The prompt is constant across samples, focusing specifically on forest segmentation. The dataset is intended for evaluating segmentation models in remote sensing and forestry applications.

context.semantics: Input satellite or aerial image of natural landscapes, serving as the primary visual context for segmentation. It contains forest and non-forest areas that the model must distinguish.

question.semantics: A short imperative instruction asking to segment the forest area in the corresponding image, guiding the segmentation task.

mask.semantics: Output binary segmentation mask image delineating forest regions in the input image; it serves as the ground-truth target for the segmentation task.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of an input satellite/aerial image (input.image_file), a short text instruction (input.prompt) asking to segment the forest area, and an output segmentation mask (output.map_file). The image serves as context; the prompt specifies the segmentation target; the mask provides the corresponding forest/non-forest pixel-level annotation.
